observation.visible_text:
Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Getting started › Quickstart Quickstart · 5 minutes From zero to a working app. In the next five minutes you'll install Runeforge, build a counter, build a todo list, and wire up an async fetcher. By the end you'll have used 90% of the API. Prerequisites: Node 20+ (or Bun). The examples use React but everything maps 1:1 to Solid, Svelte, Vue, and vanilla JS. Step 1 · Install Create a fresh app with whatever template you like. Then install Runeforge and the React adapter. # inside your app directory npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Step 2 · A counter store The smallest useful store has one piece of state and one action. Both are inferred from the object you pass to forge(). // stores/counter.ts import { forge } from "runeforge"; export const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { increment: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), decrement: (s) => ({ count: s.count - 1 }), reset: () => ({ count: 0 }), }, }); Use it in a component with useStore: // Counter.tsx import { useStore } from "@runeforge/react"; import { counter } from "./stores/counter"; export function Counter() { const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); return (

{count}

); } Notice three things: No provider. The store is just an import — it's already global. The component subscribes to a selector (s.count), not the whole store. If another part of state changed, this component would not re-render. Actions are called like ordinary methods. There's no dispatch(). Step 3 · A todo list (and a derived store) For richer state, use a slice for todos and another for the filter. Then derive a third store that combines them. // stores/todos.ts import { forge, derive } from "runeforge"; export const todos = forge({ state: { items: [] as { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }[] }, actions: { add: (s, text: string) => ({ items: [...s.items, { id: Date.now(), text, done: false }] }), toggle: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.map(t => t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t) }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => t.id !== id) }), clear: (s) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => !t.done) }), }, }); export const filter = forge({ state: { mode: "all" as "all" | "active" | "done" }, actions: { setMode: (s, mode) => ({ mode }), }, }); // derive() runs only when its inputs change. export const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => { if (f.mode === "all") return t.items; if (f.mode === "active") return t.items.filter(x => !x.done); return t.items.filter(x => x.done); }); In the component, you subscribe to the derived store the same way you subscribe to a regular one: const visible = useStore(visibleTodos); return visible.map(t => ); Step 4 · Async (the easy way) Async work belongs in effects. Effects can read and write any store, await whatever they want, and report status into a status field. Runeforge ships an asyncSlice() helper that gives you a typed status object for free. import { forge, asyncSlice } from "runeforge"; export const users = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice() }, actions: { async load(s) { if (s.status === "loading") return s; try { const r = await fetch("/api/users"); const data = await r.json(); return { status: "ready", data, error: null }; } catch (e) { return { status: "error", data: null, error: e.message }; } }, }, }); Inside the component: const { status, data, error } = useStore(users); useEffect

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) ☀ ★ 18.4k Docs › Examples Examples Apps you can fork. Self-contained example apps. React 34 LOC beginner Todo list with persistence Add / toggle / delete todos. State persists to localStorage with one option. React 88 LOC beginner Async fetcher with retry asyncSlice() pattern. Loads users with exponential-backoff retry on failure. Vue 3 110 LOC intermediate Multi-step form (typed) Uses formSlice() to manage values, errors, touched state, and submission. React 210 LOC intermediate Optimistic comments Show comments instantly, roll back on server error. Uses derive() + middleware. Solid 180 LOC intermediate Realtime presence WebSocket push updates per-user presence and merges into store. Svelte 5 240 LOC intermediate Routing-aware state Read URL params into a store; navigation is just an action. React 160 LOC advanced Undo / redo with snapshots Time-travel using built-in snapshot support. Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z. React 320 LOC advanced Server-side rendered shop Full SSR + hydration of multiple stores. Includes server-only state. React (Next 15) 460 LOC advanced Markdown editor with autosave Debounced autosave middleware, file-system adapter, and conflict detection. Vanilla JS 420 LOC advanced Spreadsheet with cross-cell formulas Each cell is a derived store; recompute graph triggered by edits. Solid 480 LOC advanced Drag-and-drop kanban (SSR) Move cards between columns; renders identically on server and client. React (Next 15) 440 LOC
